translationRepairs: In the early Qianyuan period he passed the special examination, was made collator to the Crown Prince, and served in turn as magistrate of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian counties.
In the early Qianyuan period he passed the special examination, was made collator to the Crown Prince, and served in turn as county defender of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian.
歷…三縣尉 names the county defender (縣尉), not the magistrate (縣令). The proposed office is right, but the parenthetical (wei) is unnecessary in running English.
At the beginning of the Qianyuan era, he passed the special examination and was appointed Crown Prince's collator; he served successively as county magistrate of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian.
At the beginning of the Qianyuan era, he passed the special examination and was appointed Crown Prince's collator; he served successively as county defender of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian.
The literal line likewise renders 三縣尉 as county magistrate; county defender matches the Chinese office.

Han Huang, commissioner observing the eastern and western Zhejiang circuits, recruited him as investigating officer and memorialized to make him Palace Diarist and inner attendant, with duty as supply commissioner.

Han Huang, commissioner observing the eastern and western Zhejiang circuits, recruited him as investigating officer and memorialized to make him Palace Attendant Censor and inner attendant, with duty as supply commissioner.
殿中侍御史 is a palace attendant censor, not the diarist 起居郎; the replacement restores the office named in the memorial appointment.

Han Huang, observation commissioner of the eastern and western circuits of Zhejiang, recruited him as investigating officer; he memorialized to appoint him Palace Diarist, inner attendant, and supply commissioner.

Han Huang, observation commissioner of the eastern and western circuits of Zhejiang, recruited him as investigating officer; he memorialized to appoint him Palace Attendant Censor, inner attendant, and supply commissioner.
The same 殿中侍御史 is mistranslated as Palace Diarist in the literal field; Palace Attendant Censor is accurate.

Men like Yingzhen are everywhere. Even if Yang Xiong and Du Fu were reborn, they could not comfort the people and command the armies while achieving a parental rule of kindness or the discipline of proper formations and army law.'

Men like Yingzhen are everywhere. Even if Yang Hu and Du Yu were reborn, they could not comfort the people and command the armies while achieving a parental rule of kindness or the discipline of proper formations and army law.'
羊、杜 in a speech about comforting the people and commanding armies are the Western Jin governors Yang Hu and Du Yu, not Yang Xiong and Du Fu.

Where men like Yingzhen exist everywhere, even if Yang Xiong and Du Fu were reborn, in comforting the people and commanding the three armies they could certainly not achieve a parental government of kindness and ease or the discipline of army law and good formations.'

Where men like Yingzhen exist everywhere, even if Yang Hu and Du Yu were reborn, in comforting the people and commanding the three armies they could certainly not achieve a parental government of kindness and ease or the discipline of army law and good formations.'
The literal English repeats the same false identification of 羊、杜; Yang Hu and Du Yu are the pair implied by the military-government allusion.
Nai often felt that the Ministry of Rites did not select talent as well as it might, and wrote to Selection Attendant Song Yu, saying:
Nai often felt that the Ministry of Personnel did not select talent as well as it might, and wrote to Selection Attendant Song Yu, saying:
文部 here governs 選才 and a letter to the 知銓舍人, so it is the Tianbao renaming of the Ministry of Personnel, not the Ministry of Rites.
Nai often considered that the Ministry of Rites' selection of talent was not fully adequate and therefore sent a letter to Selection Attendant Song Yu, saying:
Nai often considered that the Ministry of Personnel's selection of talent was not fully adequate and therefore sent a letter to Selection Attendant Song Yu, saying:
The literal field makes the same 文部 error; Personnel is required by the selection-bureau context.
Today the Ministry of Rites begins by weighing talent and ends by conferring office. Knowing men and placing them in office is therefore a weighty charge.
Today the Ministry of Personnel begins by weighing talent and ends by conferring office. Knowing men and placing them in office is therefore a weighty charge.
今夫文部…掄材…授位 continues the same personnel-selection topic; Rites would be 禮部.
Now the Ministry of Rites begins with weighing talent and ends with conferring office—thus to know men and assign them to office is a weighty charge.
Now the Ministry of Personnel begins with weighing talent and ends with conferring office—thus to know men and assign them to office is a weighty charge.
The literal line repeats 文部 as Rites; the ministry that weighs talent and confers office is Personnel.
Though possessed of utmost virtue, if judged by glib talk they would rank below a miser.
Though possessed of utmost virtue, if judged by glib talk they would rank below a petty bailiff.
嗇夫 is the glib petty official of the classical anecdote, not a miser (嗇 as stinginess); petty bailiff restores the office and the point about judging men by talk.
Though possessing utmost virtue, if taken by glib talk they would not even equal a miser.
Though possessing utmost virtue, if taken by glib talk they would not even equal a petty bailiff.
The literal field makes the same 嗇夫 error; the contrast is with a talkative minor official, not a miser.
He became Palace Diarist, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.
He became Palace Attendant Censor, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.
改殿中侍御史 is again Palace Attendant Censor, not Palace Diarist.
He was changed to Palace Diarist, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, all while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.
He was changed to Palace Attendant Censor, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, all while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.
The literal appointment list copies the same 殿中侍御史 mistranslation; the proposed office name is correct.
Soon he was transferred to Left Supplementation Censor.
Soon he was transferred to Left Rectifier of Omissions.
左補闕 is a remonstrance post, not a censor, so dropping Censor is required. It is not 左拾遺, which this chapter already renders Reminder; Rectifier of Omissions is the office 補闕 names.
Soon he was transferred to Left Supplementation Censor.
Soon he was transferred to Left Rectifier of Omissions.
The literal line has the same false censor label for 左補闕; Reminder would collapse it with 拾遺, so Rectifier of Omissions is the accurate office name.
Kuanfu's younger brother Duanfu was a Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, famous for opposing Wei Shou's posthumous title proposal.
Kuanfu's younger brother Duanfu was an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, famous for opposing Wei Shou's posthumous title proposal.
a Erudite is ungrammatical before a vowel sound; an erudite is the needed article fix and does not change the office 太常博士.
When Daizong ascended the throne, Gao was summoned to court and rose to Drafting Attendant and Censor-in-Chief.
When Daizong ascended the throne, Gao was summoned to court and rose to Supervising Secretary and Vice Censor-in-Chief.
給事中 is Supervising Secretary, not Drafting Attendant (中書舍人), and 御史中丞 is Vice Censor-in-Chief, not Censor-in-Chief (御史大夫).
When Daizong ascended the throne, he was summoned to court and rose through offices to Drafting Attendant and Censor-in-Chief.
When Daizong ascended the throne, he was summoned to court and rose through offices to Supervising Secretary and Vice Censor-in-Chief.
The literal field repeats both office errors for 給事中 and 御史中丞; the proposed titles match the Chinese.
His remonstrance displeased the throne and he was demoted to senior administrator of Shaozhou, then reappointed Drafting Attendant.
His remonstrance displeased the throne and he was demoted to senior administrator of Shaozhou, then reappointed Supervising Secretary.
復拜為給事中 is a reappointment as Supervising Secretary, not Drafting Attendant.
For remonstrance that missed the emperor's intent he was demoted to senior administrator of Shaozhou and later reappointed Drafting Attendant.
For remonstrance that missed the emperor's intent he was demoted to senior administrator of Shaozhou and later reappointed Supervising Secretary.
The literal reappointment likewise mistranslates 給事中; Supervising Secretary is correct.
When Fu moved to govern Hua and Hua, Pingzhong continued as his staff officer.
When Fu moved to govern Hua Prefecture in Shaanxi and Hua Prefecture in Henan, Pingzhong continued as his staff officer.

華州 and 滑州 are two prefectures whose English names collide as Hua. Repeating Hua Prefecture without the graphs still conceals the distinction the Chinese marks. English geographic qualifiers disambiguate the homophonous prefecture names without embedding Chinese text in the English replacement.
When Fu moved to govern Hua and Hua prefectures, Pingzhong still served as staff officer.
When Fu moved to govern Hua Prefecture in Shaanxi and Hua Prefecture in Henan, Pingzhong still served as staff officer.

Huazhou and Huazhou still spell both 華州 and 滑州 identically; the graphs must be kept so the two postings remain distinct. English geographic qualifiers disambiguate the homophonous prefecture names without embedding Chinese text in the English replacement.
Inner attendant Tu Tu Chenghui served as pacification commissioner against Zhen Prefecture and returned without success.
Inner attendant Tutu Chengcui served as pacification commissioner against Zhen Prefecture and returned without success.
吐突承璀 is the eunuch surname Tutu plus given name Chengcui; Tu Tu Chenghui both splits the surname and misreads 璀.
The inner attendant Tu Tu Chenghui served as pacification commissioner, campaigned against Zhen Prefecture, and returned without achievement.
The inner attendant Tutu Chengcui served as pacification commissioner, campaigned against Zhen Prefecture, and returned without achievement.
The literal name repeats Tu Tu Chenghui for 吐突承璀; Tutu Chengcui is the correct segmentation and reading.
Xianyang county magistrate Yuan Dan clashed with a military garrison. The soldiers acted without cause, slandered him freely, and Dan was punished instead.
Xianyang county defender Yuan Dan clashed with a military garrison. The soldiers acted without cause, slandered him freely, and Dan was punished instead.
咸陽縣尉 is the county defender, not the magistrate 縣令.
Xianyang county magistrate Yuan Dan disputed with a military garrison; the soldiers were without reason, then wantonly slandered and accused him, and Dan in turn was punished.
Xianyang county defender Yuan Dan disputed with a military garrison; the soldiers were without reason, then wantonly slandered and accused him, and Dan in turn was punished.
The literal field makes the same 縣尉/縣令 error; county defender is the office named.
Tinglao and his colleagues entered the inner gate and said: "We observe that recent appointments often bypass the Secretariat's recommendations and are issued directly by imperial announcement.

Tinglao and his colleagues entered the council hall to memorialize and said: "We observe that recent appointments often bypass the Secretariat's recommendations and are issued directly by imperial announcement.
入閣奏事 is attendance at the inner-court audience to memorialize, not merely walking through a physical inner gate; the proposed wording restores 奏事.
Shu Yuanshang replied: "Recently there has been too much construction in the palace."
Shu Yuanbao replied: "Recently there has been too much construction in the palace."
舒元褒 is Shu Yuanbao; 褒 is bao, not shang.
Shu Yuanshang replied: "Recently palace construction is too extensive."
Shu Yuanbao replied: "Recently palace construction is too extensive."
The literal name repeats Yuanshang for 元褒; Yuanbao is the correct reading.
Yuanshang could not answer. Tinglao stepped forward: "We are remonstrating officials. Whatever we hear, we ought to report it.
Yuanbao could not answer. Tinglao stepped forward: "We are remonstrating officials. Whatever we hear, we ought to report it.
The shortened 元褒 must stay Yuanbao, matching 舒元褒 in the preceding sentence.
Yuanshang could not answer; Tinglao stepped forward and said: "Our office is that of remonstrating officials; whatever we hear, we ought to submit memorials.
Yuanbao could not answer; Tinglao stepped forward and said: "Our office is that of remonstrating officials; whatever we hear, we ought to submit memorials.
The literal shortened name likewise misreads 元褒 as Yuanshang; Yuanbao is required.
In year 5 he was removed from the Hanlin post but kept his nominal rank. Rangyi was removed as well because of Tinglao and kept only his post as vice director of the Service Office.
In year 5 he was removed from the Hanlin post but kept his nominal rank. Rangyi was removed as well because of Tinglao and kept only his post as vice director of the Bureau of Operations.
職方員外郎 is vice director of the Bureau of Operations, not a generic Service Office.
In the fifth year he was removed from office but kept his nominal rank; Rangyi also because of Tinglao was removed from office and kept only vice director of the Service Office.
In the fifth year he was removed from office but kept his nominal rank; Rangyi also because of Tinglao was removed from office and kept only vice director of the Bureau of Operations.
The literal retained office repeats Service Office for 職方員外郎; Bureau of Operations is the named bureau.
Tan ordered households simply to weave and deliver payment, not minding the deadline; if they violated it he would merely forfeit the magistrate's salary.
Tan ordered households simply to weave and deliver payment, not minding the deadline; if he violated it he would merely forfeit the magistrate's salary.

違之不過罰令俸耳 means Tan would only forfeit the magistrate's salary if the deadline were breached; 既成而輸，坦亦坐罰 confirms he, not the households, took the fine. The original they makes the villagers the violators.
Pei Jun was Grand Mentor and stood out of rank in court assembly. Tan asked him to withdraw, but Jun refused.
Pei Jun was Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and stood out of rank in court assembly. Tan asked him to withdraw, but Jun refused.
僕射 is the vice director of the Department of State Affairs, not Grand Mentor (太傅).
Pei Jun was Grand Mentor and in court rank exceeded his proper place; Tan requested that he withdraw, but Jun did not accept.
Pei Jun was Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and in court rank exceeded his proper place; Tan requested that he withdraw, but Jun did not accept.

Tan said: "When Yao Nanzhong was Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, the precedent was the same."
姚南仲為僕射 is the same pushe office, not Grand Mentor.
Tan said: "When Yao Nanzhong was Grand Mentor, the precedent was thus."
Tan said: "When Yao Nanzhong was Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, the precedent was thus."
The literal quotation repeats Grand Mentor for 僕射; Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs is correct.
Soon afterward Tan was demoted to Right Subvisor. Contemporaries blamed Jun.
Soon afterward Tan was demoted to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent. Contemporaries blamed Jun.
右庶子 is Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, not Subvisor.
Soon afterward he was removed and made Right Subvisor; contemporaries blamed Jun.
Soon afterward he was removed and made Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent; contemporaries blamed Jun.
The literal demotion repeats Subvisor for 右庶子; the heir-apparent household office is the one named.

Within a month he was sent out as Xuancheng-She-Chi observation commissioner.
旬月 is an interval of about a month, not a strict ten days; the following appointment after 尋罷 fits within a month, and the idiomatic rendering is the accurate sense.
